title: toxicoscordion venenosum var. gramineum
intro: Toxicoscordion venenosum var. gramineum, commonly known as Western poison oak, is a plant species that is native to western North America. It has been used in traditional medicine for its health benefits, including its potential to support immune function and reduce inflammation. The therapeutic actions of Western poison oak include anti-inflammatory, antiviral, and antimicrobial properties, which contribute to its traditional use in treating various health conditions. The bioactive constituents of Western poison oak include alkaloids, saponins, and flavonoids, which have been shown to possess antioxidant and anti-inflammatory activities.
